newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South Afrian shares were buoyant at the close of a quiet day's trade after riding high on the back of Wall Street's gains on Friday and central bank governor Chris Stals' talk of a possible interest rate cut late in the year.

But a slip in the rand to 4.50 bid on the dollar -- its weakest level in four months -- stole some limelight from the industrials, while bullion's steady grip on $343 an ounce level failed to inspire gold shares, they added.

"The fall in the rand has put a little bit of a damper on the market, especially in the industrials. It's obviously going to help the gold shares, slightly I would say...but they are not going to run away," one dealer said.
The industrial index ended up 42.0 points at 8,519.2, the gold index gained 5.7 points to 1,181.3 and the all-share index rose 34.2 points to 7,296.4.
Advancing issues led decliners by 226 to 139 and 148 issues were unchanged. There were 35 new highs and 16 new lows recorded during the day.
Dealers said volumes on the day were good with around 906 million rand worth of shares traded.
They said despite slight worries about the currency's stability the market would continue its recent surge and was also seen taking a cue from Wall Street's drive to scale new highs.
Wall Street firmed sharply in early New York trade on Monday.

"We had a very good market last week and I think...if the Dow finishes very firm we'll probably see our market continue up on the back of that, but if it's down I think we'll see a little bit of weakness after this run-off," one dealer said, adding that sentiment was still bullish.
"Sentiment is positive, but the currency does concern me a little bit," he added.
Among the day's features were Genbel Securities which ended down 125 cents at 56.75 rand on a bookover deal worth around 198 million rand.

Large trade was also seen in Barlows which added 55 cents to 48.40 rand on a volume of nearly a million shares and Dimension Data added 10 cents to 16.30 rand following an earlier bookover deal of a million shares worth around 21 million rand.
Most yellow metal stocks did not react enthusiastically to the weaker rand, which pushed up the rand gold price.
Kloof ended down 10 cents at 29.55 rand and Vaal Reefs dipped 25 cents to close at 271.50 rand.
"Golds have been pretty quiet. They are a little bit in limbo at the moment and I don't think people are going to go rushing in," one dealer said.
The weak currency also dampened near-dated share futures which had started firm on a strong Wall Street overnight.
The June all-share contract was last at 6,570/90 from 6,553, the gold contract was at 800/32 from 832 and the industrial contract at 8,170/76 from 8,160.
